theme: The 72-Hour Rule: Why Post-Event Follow-Through Makes or Breaks ROI

linkedin.text:
Most event post-mortems happen too late to be useful.

By the time the debrief deck is ready, the emotional momentum has cooled, the survey response rate has dropped, and the story that could have justified next year's budget is already fading.

After 16 years and 1,500+ events produced globally, here's the pattern we see in events that deliver measurable ROI versus ones that don't:

The difference is rarely the venue, the speaker, or the production quality. It's whether the post-event 72-hour window was planned in advance or left to improvisation.

High-performing event owners treat the first three days post-event as part of the event itself — with assigned owners, pre-built templates, and a clear distribution chain for feedback, content, and next steps.

If you're an HR or marketing leader heading into a major event this quarter, build the post-event protocol into your brief before you brief the production company. You'll thank yourself on day 73.

Happy to share the post-event checklist framework we use with clients — DM me and I'll send it over.

instagram.text:
The event ended. Now what? 👇

The 72 hours after an event are worth more than most teams realise — and most teams don't plan for them at all.

We've produced 1,500+ events across 130+ destinations. The ones with the strongest ROI stories? They built the post-event plan before the event happened.

Surveys sent within 48 hours. Highlight content distributed internally by hour 72. Leadership debrief scheduled before participants even land home.

Momentum is perishable. Capture it on a deadline.

facebook.text:
Here's the expert tip most event budgets forget to fund: what happens in the 72 hours after the event ends.

The keynote landed. The gala dinner was stunning. Participants are flying home energized. And then... silence. No structured debrief. No captured momentum. No data handed back to the team who approved the budget.

After producing 1,500+ events across 130+ destinations, we've seen it consistently — the companies that build a post-event communication and feedback loop before the event date lock in measurable outcomes. The ones that wing it post-event lose the ROI story they worked months to create.

The 72-hour window is when memory is fresh, sentiment is high, and action is possible. That's when surveys go out, highlight reels get shared internally, and next steps get assigned — not six weeks later.

What does your post-event follow-through process look like? Drop it in the comments — we're always curious how other teams handle this.
